challenged_mechanism: Localize a unit-set marginal into arbitrarily many small fragments, normalize each fragment to a probability density, apply a local theorem with an unbounded dependence on the normalized density cap, and expect fragment weights alone to recover a universal constant.
counterexample: For E_N=union_{k=1}^N[2(k-1)/N,(2k-1)/N], each fragment has mass 1/N but normalized density cap N. A local constant C F(cap) therefore averages to C F(N), and a product penalty prod_i cap_i^{theta_i} averages to prod_i N_i^{theta_i}. If any such dependence is unbounded, arbitrary fragmentation destroys universality even though E_N is contained in [0,2].
replacement: Keep local estimates linear in the unnormalized submeasure mass, prove the weighted average before normalization, or select the active original-coordinate block before localizing the outside law. The assigned partner singular-payoff theorem separately localizes the half-Riesz supremum exactly to compact finite-fragment indicators.
